later_events.mechanism: further_exemption_by_new_order: EO 11642 (signed 1972-02-01, 37 FR 2565) recites this order and exempts MacIntyre further until February 28, 1973. It has no effective-date wording, so its signing date is recorded. It is a new grant overlapping the last four weeks of this order's term; it does not revoke, shorten or amend this order.

clauses.reason: Executive Order 11568 (35 FR 17703, signed 1970-11-16), under 5 U.S.C. 8335(c), exempts A. Everette MacIntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, from compulsory retirement for age until February 29, 1972. The order ends by its own terms: the stated date is recorded as 1972-02-29, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until-dates). Actor: Executive Order 11568 itself. The cited source is the order's own held text, which contains the words until February 29,1972. Later event: Executive Order 11642, signed 1972-02-01, further exempts MacIntyre until February 28, 1973; it is a new grant with its own date and quote and does not revoke or shorten this order. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11568 (35 FR 17703, Federal Register of November 18, 1970; the govinfo PDF text layer, whose heading reads 11568 with the name garbled as MadNTYRE), Exempting A. Everette MacIntyre from compulsory retirement for age, signed by Richard Nixon and dated November 16, 1970 (filed November 16, 1970); number, date and subject agree with the census register, and the text of Executive Order 11642 independently names this order by number and date. Inventory: two recitals (MacIntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, will become subject to compulsory retirement under 5 U.S.C. 8335 during February 1971; the public interest requires the exemption) and one operative command exempting him from compulsory retirement for age until February 29, 1972. The dossier's single whole-order clause matches. Lifecycle: the exemption ends by its own terms on the stated date. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on until-dates the end is recorded inclusive, 1972-02-29 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading is that it ends when that day begins. Later event: Executive Order 11642, signed 1972-02-01 (37 FR 2565), recites this order and exempts MacIntyre further, until February 28, 1973; it is a new grant that overlaps the last four weeks of this one, does not revoke or shorten it, and is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote, not as this order's end. Searches: the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit for this order; the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note search records one hit, the later further exemption; the held-text person-name search records no other hit. The dossier's missing item for the target provision of EO 11642 is resolved by reading EO 11642 in full: it is a further grant, not an amendment of this order's text.
